powers: make or authorize making the state liable for the payment of the principal of and interest on obligations of the port of New York authority
limits: shall not exceed one hundred million dollars at any time

a10-s8.plain: Notwithstanding the rest of the constitution, the legislature may by law, without a popular vote, make the state liable for bonds and notes of a public corporation financing industrial or manufacturing plants under section eight of article seven, up to nine hundred million dollars at any one time.
powers: make or authorize making the state liable for the payment of the principal of and interest on bonds of a public corporation
limits: shall not at any one time exceed nine hundred million dollars

a11-s1.plain: The legislature must maintain and support a system of free common schools where all the children of the state may be educated.
rights: wherein all the children of this state may be educated

a11-s2.plain: The corporation created in 1784 as The Regents of the University of the State of New York continues as The University of the State of New York, governed by at least nine regents. The legislature may increase, modify or diminish its corporate powers.
powers: which may be increased, modified or diminished by the legislature

a11-s3.plain: The state and its subdivisions may not use or allow use of their property, credit or public money to aid any school controlled by a religious denomination or teaching denominational doctrine, except for examination or inspection. The legislature may provide transportation of children to and from any school.
powers: the legislature may provide for the transportation of children to and from any school or institution of learning
limits: shall use its property or credit or any public money, or authorize or permit either to be used, directly or indirectly, in aid or maintenance

a12-s1.plain: All persons within the state are obliged to defend and protect the state and the United States. The legislature must provide for discharging this obligation and for maintaining and regulating an organized militia.

a13-s1.plain: Legislators and executive and judicial officers must take the prescribed oath to support both constitutions and faithfully discharge their duties. No other oath or test may be required for public office, though party committees and conventions may provide by rule for equal representation of the sexes on party committees.
powers: may, by rule, provide for equal representation of the sexes on any such committee
may, by rule, provide for equal representation of the sexes on any committee of such party
limits: no other oath, declaration or test shall be required as a qualification for any office of public trust

a13-s2.plain: When the constitution does not set the length of an office, it may be declared by law; otherwise the office is held at the pleasure of the appointing authority.
powers: it may be declared by law

a13-s3.plain: The legislature must provide for filling vacancies. A person appointed to an elective office serves only until the political year after the next annual election, but boards of education vacancies may be filled until the next regular school district election.
limits: no person appointed to fill a vacancy shall hold his or her office by virtue of such appointment longer than the commencement of the political year next succeeding the first annual election after the happening of the vacancy

a13-s4.plain: The political year and legislative term begin on January 1, and the legislature must assemble every year on the first Wednesday after the first Monday in January.

a13-s5.plain: The law must provide for removing for misconduct or malversation in office all non-judicial officers elected at general elections whose powers and duties are not local or legislative, and for filling the resulting vacancies.

a13-s6.plain: The legislature may declare when any office shall be deemed vacant, where this constitution makes no provision for that purpose.
powers: The legislature may declare the cases in which any office shall be deemed vacant

a13-s7.plain: State officers named in this constitution receive a compensation fixed by law, which shall not be increased or diminished during their term, and they may not receive any fees, perquisites of office or other compensation.
limits: which shall not be increased or diminished during the term for which he or she shall have been elected or appointed
nor shall he or she receive to his or her use any fees or perquisites of office or other compensation

a13-s8.plain: Elections of city officers, including supervisors, and of county officers in a county wholly included in a city are held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in an odd-numbered year, and their terms end at the end of an odd-numbered year. Judicial officers are excluded.

a13-s13.plain: Registers, sheriffs, county clerks and district attorneys are chosen by the electors; the governor may remove them after charges and a hearing, and must remove a district attorney who fails to prosecute violations of this article. New York City may abolish certain county offices by local law.
powers: The governor may remove any elective sheriff, county clerk, district attorney or register within the term for which he or she shall have been elected
shall have power to select, draw, summon and empanel grand and petit jurors
The city of New York is hereby vested with power from time to time to abolish by local law
limits: Sheriffs shall hold no other office
The legislature shall not pass any law affecting any such matters in relation to such offices within the city of New York

a13-s14.plain: The legislature may regulate and fix the wages, salaries and hours of work, and provide for the protection, welfare and safety, of public employees and of persons employed by contractors or subcontractors working for the state or its civil divisions.
powers: The legislature may regulate and fix the wages or salaries and the hours of work or labor
make provisions for the protection, welfare and safety

a14-s1.plain: The forest preserve shall be forever kept as wild forest lands and may not be leased, sold, exchanged or taken, nor its timber sold, removed or destroyed, except for listed highways, ski trails, land exchanges, a health and safety land account and Nordic skiing trails.
powers: the state may convey to the village of Saranac Lake ten acres of forest preserve land
the state may convey to the town of Arietta twenty-eight acres of forest preserve land
may convey to International Paper Company approximately eight thousand five hundred acres of forest preserve land
may convey to Sagamore Institute Inc., a not-for-profit educational organization, approximately ten acres of land and buildings
the state may convey to the town of Arietta fifty acres of forest preserve land
the state may convey to the town of Keene, Essex county, for public use as a cemetery owned by such town, approximately twelve acres of forest preserve land
the state may convey to the town of Long Lake, Hamilton county, one acre of forest preserve land
the state may convey to National Grid up to six acres adjoining State Route 56
the legislature may authorize the settlement
the state may authorize NYCO Minerals, Inc. to engage in mineral sampling operations
the state may subsequently convey said lot 8 to NYCO Minerals, Inc.
a town, village or county may apply, pursuant to a process determined by the legislature, to the health and safety land account
is authorized on one thousand thirty-nine acres of forest preserve lands at the Mount Van Hoevenberg Olympic Sports Complex
limits: shall be forever kept as wild forest lands
They shall not be leased, sold or exchanged, or be taken by any corporation, public or private
nor shall the timber thereon be sold, removed or destroyed

a14-s2.plain: The legislature may by general laws allow up to three per centum of forest preserve lands to be used for state-owned reservoirs for municipal water supply and for the canals, after survey, notice and hearing; benefited property pays the expense and a reasonable return to the state.
powers: The legislature may by general laws provide for the use of not exceeding three per centum of such lands
limits: such work shall not be undertaken until after the boundaries and high flow lines thereof shall have been accurately surveyed and fixed
Unsanitary conditions shall not be created or continued by any such public works

a14-s3.plain: Forest and wild life conservation are state policies; the legislature may buy land outside the Adirondack and Catskill parks for them, and may authorize dedication, use or sale of small separated forest preserve parcels outside the parks, with sale moneys used only to buy more preserve land in the parks.
powers: the legislature may appropriate moneys for the acquisition by the state of land
the legislature may by appropriate legislation, notwithstanding the provisions of section one of this article, authorize
limits: except that such lands shall not be leased, sold or exchanged, or be taken by any corporation, public or private
be expended only for the acquisition of additional lands for such forest preserve

a14-s4.plain: The state's policy is to conserve natural resources and scenic beauty and encourage agricultural development; the legislature must provide for pollution and noise abatement, protection of lands and water resources, and a state nature and historical preserve that may be disposed of only by two successive sessions.
limits: they shall not be taken or otherwise disposed of except by law enacted by two successive regular sessions of the legislature

a14-s5.plain: A violation of this article may be restrained at the suit of the people or, with the consent of the supreme court in appellate division and on notice to the attorney-general, at the suit of any citizen.
rights: may be restrained at the suit of the people
at the suit of any citizen

a14-s6.plain: Where listed highways cross forest preserve land, utility lines may be buried or co-located and bicycle paths built within the highway widths as set by law, minimizing tree removal and excluding certain new natural gas or oil pipelines.
powers: be buried or co-located within the widths of such highways
be constructed and maintained within the widths of such highways
limits: shall minimize the removal of trees or vegetation
shall not include the construction of any new intrastate natural gas or oil pipelines

a15-s1.plain: The legislature shall not sell, abandon or otherwise dispose of the barge canal, its terminals, or older canal parts that function as part of it; they remain state property forever, though the legislature may authorize revocable permits or leases.
powers: authorizing the granting of revocable permits or leases
limits: The legislature shall not sell, abandon or otherwise dispose of the now existing or future improved barge canal
nor shall it sell, abandon or otherwise dispose of any portion of the canal system existing prior to the barge canal improvement

a15-s2.plain: The ban on disposing of canals does not apply to canal lands, terminals and structures no longer necessary or useful for canal purposes, and the legislature may authorize their sale, exchange, abandonment or other disposition.
powers: The legislature may by appropriate legislation authorize the sale, exchange, abandonment or other disposition

a15-s3.plain: Canal boats follow canal laws; the legislature must fund canal superintendence and repairs yearly and may improve the canals; contracts go to the lowest responsible price; canal sale and other canal funds go into a special revenue fund spent only on the canal.
powers: may provide for the improvement of the canals
limits: Such funds shall only be expended for the maintenance, construction, reconstruction, development or promotion of the canal

a15-s4.plain: Despite the ban on disposing of canals, the legislature may authorize leasing or transferring the barge canal to the federal government, with or without compensation, may still fund the state's share of costs, and must weigh flood control and water resource benefits in setting that share.
powers: the legislature may authorize by law the lease or transfer to the federal government of the barge canal
providing annual appropriations for the state's share

a16-s1.plain: The power of taxation shall never be surrendered, suspended or contracted away, except as to public securities. Laws delegating taxing power must specify the taxes and provide for review. Exemptions come only by general laws, and religious, educational or charitable property exemptions may not be altered or repealed.
limits: The power of taxation shall never be surrendered, suspended or contracted away
Exemptions from taxation may be granted only by general laws

a16-s2.plain: The legislature shall provide for supervising, reviewing and equalizing tax assessments, which shall never exceed full value. It may provide for village taxes to be collected by other taxing authorities and for counties to advance unpaid village taxes to villages.
limits: Assessments shall in no case exceed full value

a16-s3.plain: Intangible personal property not used in business is deemed located at the owner's domicile for taxation; trust property is not located here just because the trustee is, except for death taxation in some cases. Intangibles shall not be taxed ad valorem or by ownership excise, and undistributed profits shall not be taxed.
limits: Intangible personal property shall not be taxed ad valorem
nor shall any excise tax be levied solely because of the ownership or possession thereof
Undistributed profits shall not be taxed

a16-s4.plain: Where the state has power to tax corporations incorporated under the laws of the United States, it shall not discriminate in tax rates and method between them and similar corporations doing similar business in the state.
limits: there shall be no discrimination in the rates and method of taxation

a16-s5.plain: All salaries, wages and other compensation, except pensions, paid to officers and employees of the state and its subdivisions and agencies shall be subject to taxation.

a16-s6.plain: Notwithstanding any other provision of the constitution, the legislature may authorize a county, city, town or village to undertake public improvements to redevelop blighted areas and contract indebtedness for it, without pledging faith and credit, and must pledge the resulting increase in real estate taxes.
powers: the legislature may by law authorize a county, city, town or village, or combination thereof acting together, to undertake the development of public improvements or services

The legislature may further authorize any county, city, town or village, or combination thereof acting together, to carry out the powers and duties conferred by this section by means of a public corporation
limits: without the pledge of its faith and credit, or the faith and credit of the state

a17-s1.plain: The aid, care and support of the needy are public concerns and shall be provided by the state and its subdivisions, in the manner and by the means the legislature determines.

a17-s2.plain: The state board of social welfare continues. It must visit and inspect charitable, correctional and similar institutions receiving public funds, inspect such institutions without public funds on health, safety, treatment and training, and may make rules subject to the legislature.
powers: the state board of social welfare may make rules and regulations

a17-s3.plain: The protection and promotion of the health of the state's inhabitants are matters of public concern, and the state and its subdivisions shall provide for them as the legislature determines.

a17-s4.plain: State and local authorities may provide care and treatment of persons suffering from mental disorder or defect, as the legislature determines. The head of the department of mental hygiene shall visit and inspect all institutions used for such care.
powers: may be provided by state and local authorities

a17-s5.plain: The legislature may provide for institutions to detain persons charged with or convicted of crime and for probation and parole. A state commission of correction shall visit and inspect all institutions detaining sane adults charged with or convicted of crime.
powers: The legislature may provide for the maintenance and support of institutions for the detention of persons charged with or convicted of crime and for systems of probation and parole

a17-s6.plain: Visitation and inspection authorized in this article do not exclude other visitation and inspection authorized by law now or later.

a17-s7.plain: Notwithstanding any other provision, the legislature may authorize the state, a municipality or a public corporation to lend money or credit to regulated corporations or associations to provide hospital or other facilities for treating human disease and related conditions.
powers: the legislature may authorize the state, a municipality or a public corporation acting as an instrumentality of the state or municipality to lend its money or credit

a18-s1.plain: Subject to this article, the legislature may provide for low rent housing and nursing home accommodations for persons of low income, for clearing and rebuilding substandard and insanitary areas, and for related recreational and other facilities.
powers: the legislature may provide in such manner, by such means and upon such terms and conditions as it may prescribe for low rent housing and nursing home accommodations for persons of low income

a18-s2.plain: For housing and slum clearance purposes, the legislature may make or authorize state and local subsidies, loans and guarantees, grant tax exemptions of up to sixty years, accept federal aid, and grant eminent domain. The section defines "public corporation".
powers: make or contract to make or authorize to be made or contracted capital or periodic subsidies by the state
grant or authorize tax exemptions in whole or in part
authorize cooperation with and the acceptance of aid from the United States
grant the power of eminent domain
limits: no such exemption may be granted or authorized for a period of more than sixty years

a18-s3.plain: Article VII's rules on state debts apply to state debts for loans under this article, with exceptions on submission to the people and repayment. Laws for subsidy contracts take effect without a popular vote, subject to time and dollar limits unless the people approve.
limits: the contracting of a greater amount of debt may not be authorized prior to January first, nineteen hundred forty-two
such periodic subsidies shall not be paid for a period longer than the life of the projects assisted thereby
no contracts for periodic subsidies shall be entered into in any one year requiring payments aggregating more than one million dollars
there shall not be outstanding at any one time contracts for periodic subsidies requiring payments exceeding an aggregate of thirty-four million dollars

a18-s4.plain: The legislature may let a city, town or village borrow for this article's purposes up to two percent of its average assessed real estate valuation. Self-supporting project debt may be excluded from debt limits; subsidy contracts count as debt; and larger places exceeding other limits must levy a non-real-estate tax.
powers: the legislature may authorize any city, town or village to contract indebtedness
The legislature may confer appropriate jurisdiction on the appellate division of the supreme court
limits: no such indebtedness shall be excluded except in accordance with such determination
Such periodic subsidies shall not be contracted for a period longer than the life of the projects assisted thereby

the legislature shall not authorize any city or village having a population of five thousand or more to contract indebtedness hereunder in excess of the limitations prescribed by any other article of this constitution

a18-s5.plain: A city, town or village is liable for state loans to a public corporation acting as its instrumentality; that liability is excluded from its debt limit unless there is a default. The state may pay no added subsidy to remedy or avoid a default on such a loan.
limits: No subsidy, in addition to any capital or periodic subsidy originally contracted for in aid of any project or projects authorized under this article, shall be paid by the state

a18-s6.plain: The state may make no loan or subsidy for a project unless it conforms to a plan for clearing and rebuilding substandard areas. The legislature may add conditions. Occupancy is restricted to persons of low income, with preference to those who live or lived in the area.
powers: The legislature may provide additional conditions to the making of such loans or subsidies
limits: No loan, or subsidy shall be made by the state to aid any project unless such project is in conformity with a plan or undertaking
The occupancy of any such project shall be restricted to persons of low income

a18-s7.plain: A guarantee of a public corporation's principal and interest counts as debt equal to the unpaid principal; a guarantee of interest only counts as debt equal to the commuted value of the unpaid interest, at a four percent annual rate.

a18-s8.plain: A state agency, city, town, village or public corporation with eminent domain power for this article's purposes may be empowered by the legislature to take more property than needed, and to improve, use, lease or sell the excess.
powers: may be empowered by the legislature to take property necessary for any such purpose but in excess of that required for public use

a18-s9.plain: Subject to limits set by the legislature, the state or any city, town, village or public corporation may acquire property it deems ultimately necessary or proper for this article's purposes, even if not needed for now.
powers: may acquire by purchase, gift, eminent domain or otherwise, such property

a18-s10.plain: The legislature may make all laws necessary and proper to carry out these powers. The article extends powers rather than adding limits, but does not authorize engaging in private business other than low rent housing for persons of low income or loans to owners of multiple dwellings.
powers: The legislature is empowered to make all laws which it shall deem necessary and proper for carrying into execution the foregoing powers
limits: nothing in this article contained shall be deemed to authorize or empower the state, or any city, town, village or public corporation to engage in any private business or enterprise

a19-s1.plain: Amendments may be proposed in the legislature and go to the attorney-general for an opinion. If passed by majorities of both houses in two successive sessions with an assembly election between, they go to the people; if approved, they take effect the next January first.
powers: Any amendment or amendments to this constitution may be proposed in the senate and assembly

a19-s2.plain: Every twenty years from 1957, and when the legislature provides, voters decide whether to hold a constitutional convention. If approved, delegates are elected, set the convention's rules and officers, and any amendments they adopt go to the voters and take effect the next January first.
powers: The convention shall have the power to appoint such officers, employees and assistants as it may deem necessary
limits: no amendment to the constitution shall be submitted for approval to the electors as hereinafter provided, unless by the assent of a majority of all the delegates elected to the convention

a19-s3.plain: When a constitutional convention and the legislature each propose an amendment on the same subject and both are submitted to the people at the same time, the convention's amendment, if approved, supersedes the legislature's.

a20-s1.plain: This constitution is in force from and including January 1, 1939, except as it otherwise provides.
